A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SFPO work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including identification of retained, added, and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments, training dynamics, ablations, rollout and runtime comparisons, and GPU-memory profiling.

after.justification: v3 retains original mathematical-reasoning results and adds coding experiments, DAPO and KL-penalty comparisons, and additional compute-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The fast trajectory, interpolation, slow correction, and entropy-triggered switch to GRPO remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 adds explicit entropy-buffer bookkeeping already described in v1 Section 3.4. Applying the same mechanism to coding and DAPO does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix C.2 adds training on the 14.1k-example Skywork-OR1 Code RL dataset and evaluation on LiveCodeBench, extending actual coverage from mathematical reasoning to coding. The original mathematical training datasets and six evaluation benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained GRPO and base-model comparisons, v3 evaluates DAPO against DAPO with SFPO in Figure 12 and Table 3. Figure 11 also introduces a KL-penalty replacement for interpolation as an evaluated comparator. These substantially broaden the comparison methods.

E3.justification: The stated main mathematical evaluation settings remain stable. Added protocols include a 32K response limit for coding evaluation, explicit best-average-checkpoint selection for the DAPO comparison, and matched-wall-clock comparisons in Appendix C.5. These supplement existing evaluations; deleted hyperparameter disclosures do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds coding sensitivity tests for K and alpha, interpolation-versus-KL controls, DAPO experiments probing the zero-advantage explanation, and detailed compute-cost analysis. Conversely, v1 Appendix D's response-length, entropy, and reward trajectories for four models are removed. The original main-text ablations remain.

E5.justification: The new coding evaluation explicitly reports Pass@1 averaged over four evaluations, whereas v1 only describes repeated evaluation without a count. This adds evaluation-averaging information, not evidence of increased training runs. Neither version reports training-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results include coding peaks of 21.77 for SFPO versus 18.91 for GRPO and DAPO+SFPO versus DAPO averages of 50.56 versus 49.30 and 47.87 versus 46.48. KL-comparison and runtime results are also added, while supplementary training trajectories are removed. Table 1 corrects the DS-1.5B base average from 37.27 to 37.31; Section 4.2.1 corrects the Qwen-Math-7B and DS-7B gains to 0.83 and 2.57 without changing their underlying scores.

T1.justification: v1 gives only a verbal characterization of F(K, alpha). v3 Appendix D.4 adds a local quadratic model, positive-semidefinite Hessian and noise-correlation assumptions, spectral drift expressions, a noise-accumulation bound, and an explicit approximate definition of F in Equations 14–18. This substantially expands the mathematics, although it remains an informal analysis rather than a convergence proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a plug-compatible three-stage update, preservation of the underlying objective and rollout procedure, and improved stability and efficiency. The headline gains of up to 2.80 accuracy points, 4.93-fold fewer rollouts, and 4.19-fold faster training are retained. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds the interpretation that benefits persisting under DAPO argue against zero-advantage handling as their primary source. It also explains the higher per-iteration cost, expands the proposed connection between gradient stability and lower entropy, and conditions preferred alpha values more explicitly on K. These refine the existing mechanism and efficiency interpretations.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1 Appendix C and its training table, losing AdamW, the constant 1e-6 learning rate, minibatch size, top-p, gradient clipping, FSDP/vLLM, and explicit omission of the KL penalty. Section 4.1 also drops the H100 designation. New parameter examples, measured timings, entropy bookkeeping, an updated project address, and a code-release promise add information but do not restore the deleted training recipe.

R1.justification: Section 6 revises Iterative GRPO's characterization from primarily reward-model updating to repeated policy updates on the same rollout batch, under the heading Off-policy GRPO. The new discussion reinforces SFPO's positioning as orthogonal to GRPO-family objectives. The Kwon and Zhao implementation references are removed with the training-details section.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain intact. Changes include targeted introduction and related-work rewrites, clearer iteration terminology, a naming explanation, acknowledgments and a reproducibility statement, and revised author information. Appendix sections are replaced and expanded, but the added scientific content does not amount to wholesale narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: The appendix display content changes substantially: v1's hyperparameter Table 3 and four training-dynamics figures disappear, while v3 adds five experimental figures and a distinct DAPO results Table 3. Main Figures 1–8 retain their underlying graphics, with some resizing and caption changes, including a more informative Figure 5 caption.

improvement.justification: The coding, DAPO, and KL-penalty comparisons strengthen evidence for transferability and the interpolation mechanism, while the added timing analysis clarifies the cost of extra updates. Numerical corrections also improve accuracy. These gains are limited by deletion of the detailed training recipe and supplementary dynamics, which weakens reproducibility and supporting evidence. The new mathematical treatment remains informal. Overall, v3 provides stronger validation with a meaningful reproducibility tradeoff.
